description: Observed while proving fz-6lf.2 telemetry: one logical macro invocation emitted repeated [fz, compiler2, macro, expanded] events whenever ScopeCode or demanded function-source expansion blocked and retried. Goal: execute each logical source invocation once while its quoted call, source-visible caller scope, and retained macro backend are unchanged; retain the immediate expanded root so downstream recursive waits resume without replaying compile-time effects. Signal: adjacent tests force item, body, pipe, and capture retries and assert one event per call identity; macro-product tests prove unchanged and equal reproduction reuse the result, while changed quoted input, changed retained backend content, and product retirement invalidate it. Strategy: one World-owned expansion memo keyed by rooted invocation identity and stable caller scope, with a weak reference to the retained backend allocation; retirement clears its entries. Each quoted heap also memoizes deterministic sugar rewrites so synthesized descendant identities remain stable without becoming a second authority. Function-body expansion removes only its transient __ENV__ splice through ScopeSnapshot::with_namespace.
title: Memoize macro expansion across blocked retries
